item.content:encoded: Am I the only one that was a little creeped out by the "DOES NOT RETAIN COMPLEX INFORMATION AFTER CYCLE IS COMPLETED" bit? Just a sort of vague sense of unease, like whoever was making these things had to be up to something bad. They knew they were making a sentient video game character (so it couldn't have been some sort of whimsical pet project; that shit involves some powerful mojo of some sort) and the issue was that it didn't retain itself across all cartridges (or at least through all replays- I assume through all cartridges since Lucas seems to retain simple information like his name through all versions of himself- the implication being that the complex information is also supposed to be retained through all versions of himself). Like I get the feeling that Lucas was supposed to be something sinister and horrible, but whoever was doing it never managed to complete whatever it was they were trying to do. So I got this slight sense of unease at the end with what was otherwise a mostly charming (if slightly sad) entry.
Good job on 100 upvotes this article certainly deserves it.

item.content:encoded:
I love pieces like these that show that not all SCPs are malicious or otherwise dangerous (unless this one's hiding something really well). I also enjoy video-game-based SCPs like these when they're done right - which in my opinion, this one is: It's not too long or too short for what it is, gets across all of the information the reader needs (it feels complete), and held my attention the entire way to the end, all without being egregiously reliant on gamer speak; what's present is entertaining because it's properly confined - which is important to a document that otherwise needs to sound official (which it also succeeds at, in my opinion).
This gets my +1.

I think this may be the best video game-based SCP we've had. There's some ineffable quality to it, maybe that you passed a bunch of normal pitfalls over: it's a glitch instead of all the games, it doesn't work in ROMs, it's self-aware but only to a point, it's friendly. I love that it helps you beat the game at the cost of itself, that really gives it a lot of character.

I was going to critique the chatlog, but then you had this:

>Not using lucas
Casual detected

Love it.
